correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite J_A,J_B, the twisted Choi matrix is Gamma C where Gamma=J_A^T tensor J_B is a Hermitian involution. Ordinary CP and J-CP require C>=0 and Gamma C>=0. Hermiticity implies commutation; positivity on the Gamma-negative eigenspace forces C to vanish there. This proves strong intertwining and the Kraus support condition, with converse immediate. Trace preservation gives sector-population conservation. For qubit Z this forces diagonal Kraus, yielding exactly |c|<=1. The Pauli distance lower bound is the trace-norm change of |0><0|, 2(qX+qY); the explicit compatible I/Z mixture attains the same diamond-norm upper bound by a two-term channel-difference decomposition.

value.rationale: A central ambiguity in indefinite-metric quantum information is which J-positive channels remain ordinary physically implementable channels. The theorem gives a complete finite-dimensional structural answer rather than a sufficient test: physical compatibility forces exact fundamental-sector conservation. For qubits it gives a full disk classification, and the sharp Pauli-channel diamond distance quantifies the operational penalty of symmetry-flipping X/Y faults, with an attained optimal physical approximation. This is a motivated quantitative boundary on channel models, not an arbitrary example.
